name: Post-quantum cryptography
summary: New cryptographic algorithms protect communications and signatures against attacks that future quantum computers could enable.
useCase: A bank inventories its encryption dependencies, upgrades customer connections to hybrid post-quantum key exchange and plans certificate migration.
whyNow: Standardized algorithms now allow deployment planning and interoperable products. NIST finalized its first three PQC standards in August 2024. Cloudflare reported that over half of human HTTPS traffic reaching its network used post-quantum protection by October 2025 and over 65% by April 2026. These are network-specific observations and primarily concern key exchange; signatures and older systems require additional work. NIST’s final IR8547, published October 27, makes the migration pathway more concrete. It does not measure completed deployment.

mainstream.scope: Post-quantum key exchange and planned authentication migration in new cloud, browser and regulated-enterprise systems.
mainstream.rationale: Standards and major-platform rollout make adoption likely before practical large quantum attacks are demonstrated. Cloudflare’s stated 2029 roadmap anchors an early infrastructure target. Complete replacement across long-lived embedded equipment, archives and legacy estates can extend beyond 2035, so the headline year describes new and priority deployments.

metric.name: Cloudflare human HTTPS traffic with post-quantum protection
metric.scope: Traffic reaching Cloudflare; reported threshold snapshots.
metric.limitations: Lower-bound disclosures, not exact percentages or a global internet census. This denominator excludes automated traffic. Older TLS 1.3-specific statistics have a different denominator and are deliberately not combined. Hybrid key exchange is not the same as quantum-safe authentication everywhere.
metric.futureNote: Cloudflare targets completing its platform roadmap by 2029. That is a vendor target, not a forecast that all systems or internet traffic will be fully migrated.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: No comparable production-traffic statistic identified for the defined KPI.
NIST’s continuing selection process preceded final standards; no invented deployment share is supplied.
No same-denominator human-HTTPS measurement supplied for this year.
NIST released the first three finalized PQC standards in August.
Cloudflare reported post-quantum protection for more than half of human HTTPS traffic.
The reported threshold exceeded 65%; Cloudflare published a 2029 completion roadmap.
October 27: NIST published final IR8547 on transition from vulnerable cryptography to PQC standards.

tailwinds: Standards give vendors a common implementation target.
Long confidentiality lifetimes justify migration before a cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists.
bottlenecks: Cryptographic inventories, certificate chains and old firmware create long migration programs.
Performance, key sizes, hardware constraints and algorithm agility require careful interoperability testing.
watchMetrics: Share of priority connections using standardized PQC, with key exchange and signatures measured separately.
Percentage of critical cryptographic dependencies inventoried, upgraded and independently tested.
